title: One percent
topic: how small daily improvements or declines compound over a year
promise: Small daily changes compound: one percent better every day is about thirty-seven times better after a year, one percent worse is almost nothing left.

takeaway.text: Judge a habit by where it leads in a year, not by how it feels today.

scenes.visualIdea: The number 1% alone in the middle of the frame, small and unimpressive.

scenes.narration: One better choice today changes almost nothing you can see. So most people stop.
scenes.visualIdea: A runner trains once and sees no change; the scale does not move.

scenes.narration: But improve by one percent every day for a year and you end up about thirty-seven times better. Get one percent worse every day and you are left with almost nothing.
scenes.visualIdea: Two lines start at the same point: one bends upward, one sinks toward zero.

scenes.narration: The difference stays invisible for months. Then it becomes impossible to miss.
scenes.visualIdea: The two lines stay together for months, then split apart near the end.

scenes.narration: So do not judge a habit by today. Judge it by where it takes you in a year.
scenes.visualIdea: The 1% from the opening, now with the year's curve drawn behind it.

claims.text: 1.01 to the power of 365 is about 37.8; 0.99 to the power of 365 is about 0.03.
